title: RAJESH KUMAR NIGAM versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND
judges: ["Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ravindra Maithani,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Siddhartha Sah"]

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 628 of 2026 (S/B)
Rajesh Kumar Nigam ........Petitioner

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ........Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Shubhang Dobhal, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. S.S. Chaudhary, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
Mr. B.S. Parihar, learned counsel for the respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Coram:Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
 Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
By means of instant writ petition, the petitioner seeks
the following reliefs :-
"i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing
the impugned Office Memorandum No. B.Ni./09/1207/2026/2397
dated 18.07.2026 passed by the Managing Director, Uttarakhand
Seeds and Tarai Development Corporation Ltd. (Annexure No. 1 to
this writ petition). Page No-26 to 29.
ii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to pay to the petitioner interest on the
amount of gratuity from 31.08.2017, i.e. the date on which it became
payable, till the date of actual payment, at the rate of 18% per annum
or at such rate as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit, but not less than
the rate notified under Section 7(3A) of the Payment of Gratuity Act,
1972.
iii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to pay to the petitioner interest on the
delayed payment of leave encashment, group insurance, last month's
salary and other retiral dues from 01.09.2017 till the respective dates
of actual payment, at such rate as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit.
iv. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to pay to the petitioner the balance
amount of gratuity of Rs. 4,84,993/- along with interest thereon.
v. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to pay to the petitioner the arrears of
1

2026:UHC:9080-DB
ACP for the entire period of his entitlement along with interest on the
arrears from the respective dates on which they fell due till the date of
actual payment.
vi. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to refund to the petitioner the amount
deducted from his retiral dues towards penal rent and other heads, or
in the alternative to consider waiver of penal rent under Rule 10 of the
House Allotment Rules of the Corporation by a reasoned order.
vii. Issue any other suitable writ, order or direction which this Hon'ble
Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the
case.
viii. Award the cost of the writ petition in favour of the
petitioner."
2. Heard learned counsel for the parities and perused the
record.
3. Petitioner retired as Company Secretary from respondent
no.3, Uttarakhand Seeds and Tarai Development Corporation Ltd.
on 31.08.2017. He was not paid retiral dues, including gratuity on
time. This forced him to file Writ Petition (S/B) No. 407 of 2021,
Rajesh Kumar Nigam vs. State of Uttarakhand and Others ("the
first writ petition"). The first writ petition was decided on
14.06.2024 and in paragraph 14 of the judgment, the Coordinate
bench of this Court observed as follows:
"14. In such view of the matter, the writ petitions are allowed. The act
of Uttarakhand Seeds and Tarai Development Corporation Ltd. to
withhold Gratuity, Leave Encashment, Group Insurance and other
monetary benefits of the petitioners, is declared to be illegal.
Petitioners shall be entitled to Gratuity, Leave Encashment, Group
Insurance and other monetary benefits, which shall be released by
Uttarakhand Seeds and Tarai Development Corporation Ltd. to the
petitioners, without any further delay."
4. Against this order dated 14.06.2024, the department
approached the Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP (Civil) Diary No.
23851 of 2025, Uttarakhand Seeds and Tarai Development
2

UKHC010171642026
2026:UHC:9080-DB
Corporation Limited and Others vs. Rajesh Kumar Nigam and
another. The SLP was dismissed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on
23.05.2025.
5. Thereafter, when the dues were not paid, the petitioner
was forced to file WPSB No. 158 of 2026, Rajesh Kumar Nigam vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ("the second writ petition"). By the
judgment dated 27.03.2026, passed in the second writ petition,
liberty was given to the petitioner to make a representation to the
competent authority for the remaining dues.
6. The petitioner submitted a representation, which was
rejected by the impugned order dated 18.07.2026.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that he
does not press relief nos. i. iv, v and vi. He submits that he is only
pressing relief nos. ii, i.e for payment of interest on amount of
gratuity and relief no. iii, i.e. interest on the delayed payment of
leave encashment, etc.
8. Since relief nos. i, iv, v and vi are not pressed by the
petitioner, the writ petition is dismissed qua those reliefs.
9. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that
the petitioner retired from service in the year 2017 and without any
fault on his part, he was not paid his dues on time. Therefore, he
is entitled to interest.
10. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that
under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the rate of interest is
governed by Section 7(3A) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 and
vide Notification dated 1st October, 1987, the Central Government
has provided for payment of simple interest @ ten percent per
3

UKHC010171642026
2026:UHC:9080-DB
annum by the employer to his employee in cases where the gratuity
is not paid within the specified time.
11. Mr. B.S. Parihar, learned counsel for the respondent
nos. 2 & 3 would submit that in compliance with the order of the
Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount has been paid to the petitioner
in the year 2025.
12. Interest is payable from the date when it becomes due.
In the first writ petition, in paragraph 14 of the judgment, the
Coordinate bench of this Court had categorically held that :
"The act of Uttarakhand Seeds and Tarai Development Corporation
Ltd. to withhold Gratuity, Leave Encashment, Group Insurance and
other monetary benefits to the petitioners is declared to be illegal."
13. This order has been affirmed by the Hon'ble Supreme
Court in the SLP that was preferred by respondent no. 3, which
means the petitioner was entitled to his dues on time and he was
not paid dues due to the act of the respondents. Thus, the
petitioner is entitled to simple interest @ 10% per annum w.e.f.
31.08.2017 as per Notification dated 1st October, 1987 under
Section 7(3A) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 and reasonable
interest on other dues. Therefore, the respondents shall pay simple
interest to the petitioner @ 10% per annum on the amount of
gratuity from 31.08.2017 and also pay interest on other dues from
31.08.2017 @ 6% simple interest per annum.
14. The writ petition is disposed of accordingly.
